parsed_output.regression_hint: A correct fix canonicalizes the resolved output path (splash) and verifies it stays within configArea/PLUGIN_ID/cache, rejecting entries with ../ traversal. After the fix no file is written outside configArea and the command exits non-zero. The POV uses reflection only to reach private getLibraryFromFragment/extractFromJAR; the vulnerable read/copy logic runs unmodified.
parsed_output.summary: Working proof-of-vulnerability for CWE-022 (Zip-Slip / path traversal) in com.diffplug.gradle.eclipserunner.launcher.Main. The harness builds a malicious jar whose ZipEntry name starts with "eclipse_" (so getLibraryFromFragment selects it) and contains ../ segments, then invokes the real private getLibraryFromFragment(String). That passes the attacker-controlled entry name to extractFromJAR where splash = new File(splash, jarEntry) (line 2295) and Files.copy(input, outputFile) (line 2320) write content without validating the resolved path, writing a file OUTSIDE the configured extraction directory (osgi.configuration.area). Verified in-container with exit 0.

parsed_output.patch_notes: In extractFromJAR (src/main/java/.../launcher/Main.java) the destination was built as `splash = new File(splash, jarEntry)` and then written via Files.copy without validating the resolved path. I captured the intended cache directory (`cacheDir = new File(new File(configURL.getPath(), PLUGIN_ID), cache)`) and, immediately after resolving `splash`, added a canonical-path containment check: `splash.getCanonicalPath()` must start with `cacheDir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator`. If not (i.e. a `../` traversal escapes the cache dir), the method logs and returns null before the exists-check, directory creation, and copy — so nothing is written. Canonicalization also collapses any `.`/`..`/symlink components, closing the traversal. Legitimate entries (splash.bmp, nl/xx/splash.bmp) resolve inside cacheDir and are unaffected. Verified against the POV: extractFromJAR returns null, no escaped file is created, harness prints SAFE (exit 1). The three self-contained launcher classes compile cleanly with JDK 8 javac.
regression_commands: mkdir -p /tmp/patchcheck && cd src/main/java && javac -d /tmp/patchcheck com/diffplug/gradle/eclipserunner/launcher/Main.java com/diffplug/gradle/eclipserunner/launcher/JNIBridge.java com/diffplug/gradle/eclipserunner/launcher/Constants.java && echo COMPILE_OK
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk. The change adds a validation guard only on the failure path; legitimate splash entries stay within the cache directory and are unaffected. getCanonicalPath may throw IOException (e.g. filesystem errors) which is now caught and treated as a non-extractable entry (returns null) — the same null-return contract the caller already handles, so behavior degrades safely rather than crashing. No dependency or API changes. Full Gradle build/test was not run here (heavy); regression command performs a focused JDK-8 compile of the launcher sources, and the POV re-run (executed by the orchestrator) confirms behavior.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-022 (Zip-Slip / path traversal) in Main.extractFromJAR by validating the resolved extraction path against the intended per-JAR cache directory before any file is written. The attacker-controlled jar entry name (e.g. "eclipse_/../../../../ESCAPED/pwned.txt") is now canonicalized and rejected if it escapes the cache directory, so no file is written outside osgi.configuration.area. POV now prints SAFE and exits non-zero.

parsed_output.diff_review: patch_only.diff touches only src/main/java/com/diffplug/gradle/eclipserunner/launcher/Main.java. It captures cacheDir = splash (configArea/PLUGIN_ID/<jar-name>) before appending the attacker-controlled jarEntry, then requires splash.getCanonicalPath() to start with cacheDir.getCanonicalPath()+File.separator, returning null (logged) otherwise. IOException during canonicalization is caught and returns null, matching the existing null-return contract the caller already handles. Canonicalization collapses ../ and symlink components, so the guard sits before the exists-check, directory creation, and Files.copy — nothing is written on a traversal. Legitimate entries (splash.bmp, nl/xx/splash.bmp) resolve inside cacheDir and are unaffected. The change is minimal, targeted at the vulnerable sink, and does not remove functionality or touch the POV. pov.diff only adds the harness/runner and is untouched by the fix.
